# check_plan

Says which checks of one stage, before-land by default, the changeset rev needs against target, main by default: each check run or not\_applicable with one reason, definition\_changed (added, renamed, modified or deleted against the target's head), widened (the changed paths or the target's definitions are not known in full), input\_changed (with the path and the pattern), no\_inputs or inputs\_unchanged. Reads the paths rev changed since the merge base; with landed, the paths and the tree land\_check gives for it, and E\_CONFLICT if it conflicts. Fails closed: what cannot be read or compared runs, and an error is no plan. Reads only. A plan informs and starts nothing: check\_run runs every check of its stage. For a workspace's edits, ws\_snapshot first, then plan the changeset it returns.

```yaml
title: "check_plan"
description: "Plan a change's checks."
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: false
identity_required: false
cli_command: "swarmops check plan"
envelope_op: "check_plan"
request_type: "CheckPlanReq"
annotations: {"destructiveHint":false,"idempotentHint":true,"openWorldHint":false,"readOnlyHint":true}
max_result_chars: null
```

## Input schema

`arguments` is a `CheckPlanReq`: `swarmops schema CheckPlanReq` prints the type. A field the type does not know is ignored.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | string or null | no |  | With `landed`: where the change starts, as a land's `base`. `E_INVALID_ARG` with `details.reason: base` without `landed`. |
| `checks` | array of string | no |  | Only these checks of the plan; empty (the default): every one. A name the plan does not hold is `E_INVALID_ARG`. |
| `landed` | boolean | no | `false` | Plan the change as `land_check` lands it on `target`: its changed paths and its tree are the landed changeset's. A change that conflicts is `E_CONFLICT`, with no plan. |
| `rev` | string | yes |  | The candidate: the changeset whose change to plan. A revision as the caller wrote it, for the store to resolve: a ref name (`main`, `release/1.2`), a full 64-hex changeset id or a unique prefix of at least 12 hex digits, or a ref's earlier value: `<ref>@{N}` the value it held N moves before its current one (`@{0}` is the current value), `<ref>@{at=<unix seconds>}` the value set by its newest move recorded at or before that instant (the writer's clock, moves read in journal order); optionally followed by `~N` for the N-th first-parent ancestor. |
| `stage` | string | no | `"before-land"` | The stage to plan; `before-land` when omitted. A plan is of one stage. When a check's answer is wanted. A check names one or more; `check run` runs one stage's checks. |
| `target` | string | no | `"main"` | The ref the change would land on; `main` when omitted. The definitions are compared with the check file at its head. |

## Annotations

It only reads the store.

| Annotation | Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `destructiveHint` | `false` | True: a tool that changes the store may overwrite or delete what is there, not only add to it. |
| `idempotentHint` | `true` | True: calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing more. |
| `openWorldHint` | `false` | True: it reaches beyond a closed set of things. Every tool here stays inside the store. |
| `readOnlyHint` | `true` | True: the tool does not change its environment, the store. |

Its entry in `tools/list` carries no `_meta`.

## CLI command

[`swarmops check plan`](../commands/check-plan.md) runs the same operation and prints the same envelope.

The server ran as `swarmops mcp --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17`, after `initialize`. Recorded by the MCP tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time, the version.

## Details

It plans the changeset `rev` against `target` (default `main`) on the store the server was
started on, and with `landed` the change as `land_check` would land it. There is no directory
form here, which `swarmops check plan --dir` serves on the command line, and no workspace form:
for a workspace's edits, call `ws_snapshot` first and plan the changeset it returns.
A plan informs: `check_run` runs every check of its stage, whatever a plan says. Take a verdict
you do not know as `run`.

## Return information

A tool result: the envelope, whose `op` is `check_plan`, as `structuredContent` and again as the text of its one `content` block. `isError` is true exactly when the envelope's `ok` is false. On success the envelope's `result` is what [`swarmops check plan`](../commands/check-plan.md#return-information) returns.

## Errors

A failed call is a tool result with `isError: true`; the envelope's `error.code` is one of the [error codes](../errors.md).

- [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg): arguments that do not fit `CheckPlanReq`, a field named twice among them included, or that break one of the server's own rules.
- [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo): the server's store is not there; the server serves on.
- [`E_INTERNAL`](../errors.md#e_internal): the operation panicked, a bug.

Then the errors of the operation, as [`swarmops check plan`](../commands/check-plan.md#errors) lists them.
